"title": "Synthesis, Biological Activity and Molecular Docking of New Tricyclic Series as α-glucosidase Inhibitors",
"authors": "Hatem A Abuelizz; Azman N I Nor; Iwana; Rohaya Ahmad; Anouar El-Hassane; Mohamed Marzouk; Rashad Al-Salahi",

"executive_summary": "This study addresses the global burden of diabetes, which the WHO reported to have risen from 108 million people in 1980 to 422 million, with prevalence among adults increasing from 4.7% in 1980 to 8.5% in 2014. A major limitation of clinically available α-glucosidase inhibitors such as acarbose is their gastrointestinal side effects, including flatulence and diarrhoea, which reduce patient compliance. To overcome these limitations, the researchers sought to develop new scaffolds that mimic the inhibitory mechanism without the drawbacks of sugar mimetic agents. The team synthesized 25 tricyclic 2-phenoxypyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones hybrids and evaluated their α-glucosidase inhibitory activity in vitro. The compounds were tested at equal concentrations of 100 µg/mL, with the test repeated three times for each compound to obtain the average percent inhibition. Eight compounds that exhibited more than 50% average percent inhibition were further evaluated for their IC 50 values, which were compared to that of acarbose. Two compounds, 6h and 6d, showed stronger activity than acarbose. Compound 6h exhibited the highest inhibition with an IC 50 of 104.07 µM. Molecular docking studies revealed that compound 6h inhibits α-glucosidase due to the formation of a stable ligand-α-glucosidase complex and extra hydrogen bond interactions, directed in the binding site by Trp329. The docking calculations were performed using the Autodock software package, with the protein structure downloaded from the RCSB data bank (PDB code 3W37). The binding energy of docked 6h was found to be the lowest (-10.56 kcal/mol) among the docked derivatives. This study provides a new structural insight for the development of novel α-glucosidase inhibitors that differ from the commonly employed carbasugars and can potentially be transformed into new clinical drugs for the treatment of type II diabetes. The work contributes to the growing body of research on α-glucosidase inhibitors, which have been found to have a range of biological activities beyond their antidiabetic effects, including antiviral, anticancer, and anti-inflammatory activities. The study's findings are significant because they demonstrate that the introduction of a branch to the pyrimidine scaffold through a nitrogen bridge results in a series of synthetic compounds with significant inhibitory activity against α-glucosidase. The researchers' decision to modify well-accepted scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, such as pyridine, triazole, and pyrimidine, reflects a strategic approach to drug discovery that builds on the known pharmacological activities of these scaffolds. The study's methodology is rigorous, with the use of triplicate experiments and molecular docking to provide insights into the binding modes of the target enzyme and docked synthesized derivatives. The findings have important implications for the development of new antidiabetic agents, as they demonstrate that the tricyclic series can serve as a new lead scaffold for the development of clinically effective antidiabetic drugs. Overall, this study makes a valuable contribution to the field of medicinal chemistry and drug discovery, and its findings are likely to be of interest to researchers working on the development of new treatments for diabetes and related metabolic disorders.",

summary.title: Synthesis, Biological Activity and Molecular Docking of New Tricyclic Series as α-glucosidase Inhibitors
summary.authors: Hatem A Abuelizz; Azman N I Nor; Iwana; Rohaya Ahmad; Anouar El-Hassane; Mohamed Marzouk; Rashad Al-Salahi
summary.type_of_paper: Experimental synthesis, biological screening, and molecular docking study
summary.executive_summary: This study addresses the global burden of diabetes, which the WHO reported to have risen from 108 million people in 1980 to 422 million, with prevalence among adults increasing from 4.7% in 1980 to 8.5% in 2014. A major limitation of clinically available α-glucosidase inhibitors such as acarbose is their gastrointestinal side effects, including flatulence and diarrhoea, which reduce patient compliance. To overcome these limitations, the researchers sought to develop new scaffolds that mimic the inhibitory mechanism without the drawbacks of sugar mimetic agents. The team synthesized 25 tricyclic 2-phenoxypyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones hybrids and evaluated their α-glucosidase inhibitory activity in vitro. The compounds were tested at equal concentrations of 100 µg/mL, with the test repeated three times for each compound to obtain the average percent inhibition. Eight compounds that exhibited more than 50% average percent inhibition were further evaluated for their IC 50 values, which were compared to that of acarbose. Two compounds, 6h and 6d, showed stronger activity than acarbose. Compound 6h exhibited the highest inhibition with an IC 50 of 104.07 µM. Molecular docking studies revealed that compound 6h inhibits α-glucosidase due to the formation of a stable ligand-α-glucosidase complex and extra hydrogen bond interactions, directed in the binding site by Trp329. The docking calculations were performed using the Autodock software package, with the protein structure downloaded from the RCSB data bank (PDB code 3W37). The binding energy of docked 6h was found to be the lowest (-10.56 kcal/mol) among the docked derivatives. This study provides a new structural insight for the development of novel α-glucosidase inhibitors that differ from the commonly employed carbasugars and can potentially be transformed into new clinical drugs for the treatment of type II diabetes. The work contributes to the growing body of research on α-glucosidase inhibitors, which have been found to have a range of biological activities beyond their antidiabetic effects, including antiviral, anticancer, and anti-inflammatory activities. The study's findings are significant because they demonstrate that the introduction of a branch to the pyrimidine scaffold through a nitrogen bridge results in a series of synthetic compounds with significant inhibitory activity against α-glucosidase. The researchers' decision to modify well-accepted scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, such as pyridine, triazole, and pyrimidine, reflects a strategic approach to drug discovery that builds on the known pharmacological activities of these scaffolds. The study's methodology is rigorous, with the use of triplicate experiments and molecular docking to provide insights into the binding modes of the target enzyme and docked synthesized derivatives. The findings have important implications for the development of new antidiabetic agents, as they demonstrate that the tricyclic series can serve as a new lead scaffold for the development of clinically effective antidiabetic drugs. Overall, this study makes a valuable contribution to the field of medicinal chemistry and drug discovery, and its findings are likely to be of interest to researchers working on the development of new treatments for diabetes and related metabolic disorders.

claims.description: The tricyclic series of 2-phenoxypyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones exhibits significant α-glucosidase inhibitory activity.
The aminobridge substitution of the pyrimidine ring at position 4 is responsible for the strong inhibitory activity.

Executive Summary
This study addresses the global burden of diabetes, which the WHO reported to have risen from 108 million people in 1980 to 422 million, with prevalence among adults increasing from 4.7% in 1980 to 8.5% in 2014. A major limitation of clinically available α-glucosidase inhibitors such as acarbose is their gastrointestinal side effects, including flatulence and diarrhoea, which reduce patient compliance. To overcome these limitations, the researchers sought to develop new scaffolds that mimic the inhibitory mechanism without the drawbacks of sugar mimetic agents. The team synthesized 25 tricyclic 2-phenoxypyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones hybrids and evaluated their α-glucosidase inhibitory activity in vitro. The compounds were tested at equal concentrations of 100 µg/mL, with the test repeated three times for each compound to obtain the average percent inhibition. Eight compounds that exhibited more than 50% average percent inhibition were further evaluated for their IC 50 values, which were compared to that of acarbose. Two compounds, 6h and 6d, showed stronger activity than acarbose. Compound 6h exhibited the highest inhibition with an IC 50 of 104.07 µM. Molecular docking studies revealed that compound 6h inhibits α-glucosidase due to the formation of a stable ligand-α-glucosidase complex and extra hydrogen bond interactions, directed in the binding site by Trp329. The docking calculations were performed using the Autodock software package, with the protein structure downloaded from the RCSB data bank (PDB code 3W37). The binding energy of docked 6h was found to be the lowest (-10.56 kcal/mol) among the docked derivatives. This study provides a new structural insight for the development of novel α-glucosidase inhibitors that differ from the commonly employed carbasugars and can potentially be transformed into new clinical drugs for the treatment of type II diabetes. The work contributes to the growing body of research on α-glucosidase inhibitors, which have been found to have a range of biological activities beyond their antidiabetic effects, including antiviral, anticancer, and anti-inflammatory activities. The study's findings are significant because they demonstrate that the introduction of a branch to the pyrimidine scaffold through a nitrogen bridge results in a series of synthetic compounds with significant inhibitory activity against α-glucosidase. The researchers' decision to modify well-accepted scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, such as pyridine, triazole, and pyrimidine, reflects a strategic approach to drug discovery that builds on the known pharmacological activities of these scaffolds. The study's methodology is rigorous, with the use of triplicate experiments and molecular docking to provide insights into the binding modes of the target enzyme and docked synthesized derivatives. The findings have important implications for the development of new antidiabetic agents, as they demonstrate that the tricyclic series can serve as a new lead scaffold for the development of clinically effective antidiabetic drugs. Overall, this study makes a valuable contribution to the field of medicinal chemistry and drug discovery, and its findings are likely to be of interest to researchers working on the development of new treatments for diabetes and related metabolic disorders.

Research Context
Diabetes is a growing global health problem affecting hundreds of millions of people. α-Glucosidase inhibitors are used to control postprandial hyperglycaemia by delaying carbohydrate hydrolysis. Clinically available α-glucosidase inhibitors suffer from gastrointestinal side effects that reduce patient compliance. Gastrointestinal side effects such as flatulence and diarrhoea are caused by bacterial digestion of complex carbohydrates in the colon. There is a high demand for effective antidiabetic agents that overcome the side effects of sugar mimetic agents. α-Glucosidase inhibitors have a range of biological activities beyond their antidiabetic effects. Well-accepted scaffolds such as pyridine, triazole, and pyrimidine have proven pharmacological activities. Pyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones have been reported as effective fungicidal agents. Most produced α-glucosidase inhibitors are sugar mimetics that require tedious synthesis. The valienamine moiety in acarbose mimics the oxocarbenium ion-like transition state that binds to and inhibits α-glucosidase.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central research question is whether new tricyclic scaffolds can serve as effective α-glucosidase inhibitors. The researchers hypothesized that modifying well-accepted scaffolds would yield compounds with significant inhibitory activity. The researchers predicted that introducing a branch to the pyrimidine scaffold through a nitrogen bridge would enhance inhibitory activity. The researchers hypothesized that the aminobridge substitution of the pyrimidine ring at position 4 is responsible for strong inhibitory activity. The researchers predicted that compounds with lower IC 50 values than acarbose would demonstrate superior inhibitory activity. The researchers hypothesized that molecular docking studies would reveal the binding modes of the target enzyme and docked derivatives. The researchers predicted that compound 6h would exhibit the highest inhibition due to its stable ligand-α-glucosidase complex. The researchers hypothesized that Trp329 plays a significant role in directing the ligand in the binding site. The researchers predicted that the number of established hydrogen bonds would correlate with inhibitory activity. The researchers hypothesized that the tricyclic series could serve as a new lead scaffold for clinically effective antidiabetic drugs.

Methodological Details
The study synthesized 25 tricyclic 2-phenoxypyrido[3,2-e][1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones hybrids. The α-glucosidase inhibitory assay was performed in vitro to screen the biological activity of the synthesized derivatives. The enzyme was treated with equal concentrations of 100 µg/mL of each compound. The test was repeated three times for each compound to obtain the average percent inhibition. The inhibitory activity of all tested compounds was between 30% and 63%. Eight compounds that exhibited more than 50% average percent inhibition were further evaluated for their IC 50 values. Compounds 3, 6c and 6d showed average percent inhibition of more than 60%. Compounds 2a, 2d, 6a, 6b and 6h showed average percent inhibition of more than 50% but less than 60%. Acarbose was used as a positive control to compare with the synthesized compounds. The α-glucosidase enzyme was type 1 from Baker's yeast, dissolved in phosphate-buffered saline at pH 6.5. The p-NPG substrate was prepared at a concentration of 20 mM in buffer solution. The reaction was incubated for 30 min at 37 °C, and the absorbance was measured at 405 nm. The molecular docking studies were performed using the Autodock software package. The original docked protein was downloaded from the RCSB data bank with PDB code 3W37. The binding energy of the formed complex had a relative standard deviation of less than 2.34 kcal/mol. The synthetic route involved the incorporation of a hydrazine moiety to Ncyanoimidocarbonates to generate triazoles. The reaction of compound 1 with alkyl or heteroalkyl halides gave the expected [1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-5(4H)-ones in 45-83% yields. The conversion of 3 into 4 was carried out in basic medium using benzyl bromide. The transformation of 1 into 5 was achieved employing phosphorous oxychloride as chlorinating agent in boiling benzene. The reaction of 5 with hydroxylamine HCl provided the corresponding product 6e in 63% yield. The treatment of target 5 with several aromatic amines afforded the corresponding compounds 6a-d in 60-68% yields. The chlorine was replaced in 5 by isoniazid in boiling toluene to give amidrazone 6i in good yield (74%). The hydrazinolysis of 5 in boiling ethanol produced the corresponding compound 6f. The formation of 5 was followed by NMR and IR spectroscopy, confirming the disappearance of the C=O band. The 1 H-NMR spectra of targets 1-6 were characterized by two consistent spin coupling systems. The 13 C NMR spectra of compound 3 displayed a peak resonance at 186.0 ppm due to the C=S group. The IR and NMR data confirmed the formation of N-alkylated products 2a-l. The phosphate-buffered saline was prepared at 20 °C by dissolving sodium phosphate monobasic, sodium chloride, potassium chloride, and potassium dihydrogen phosphate. The percent inhibition of α-glucosidase inhibitory activity was calculated using a specific equation. The detailed steps for the molecular docking studies were reported by Abuelizz and collaborators.

The 1,2,4-triazole intermediate B was obtained when an ethanolic solution of diphenoxy-Ncyanoimidocarbonate reacted with A in a basic medium. The reaction was carried out in a basic medium (triethylamine) at room temperature. Upon treatment of B with conc. HCl, initially at room temperature followed by heating, afforded novel compounds. The mixture was acidified with conc. HCl under ice cooling and then heated for 1-2 h at 80 °C. The product was obtained as a white amorphous powder (78%); mp: 252-254 °C. The IR spectra displayed absorption bands at 1670-1688 cm -1 due to the C=O group. Boiling equimolar amounts of target 1 and phosphorous pentasulfide in absolute pyridine furnished the desired thione (3) in excellent yield (90%). The IR and 13 C NMR spectra of compound 3 displayed a weak absorption band (1272 cm -1 ) and a peak resonance (186.0 ppm) due to the C=S group. The transformation of 1 into 5 was achieved employing phosphorous oxychloride as chlorinating agent in boiling benzene followed by treatment with a saturated basic solution. The conversion of the lactam group in 1 into an imidoyl chloride moiety (5) provided a valuable intermediate for further displacement reactions. The reaction of 5 with hydroxylamine HCl in a molar ratio of 1:2.5 in boiling pyridine provided the corresponding product 6e in 63% yield. The treatment of target 5 with several aromatic amines in pyridine in a molar ratio of 1:5 afforded the corresponding compounds 6a-d in 60-68% yields. The chlorine was replaced in 5 by isoniazid in boiling toluene to give amidrazone 6i in good yield (74%). The hydrazinolysis of 5 in boiling ethanol produced the corresponding compound 6f. The treatment of 6f with equimolar amounts of aldehydes resulted in the formation of hydrazone derivatives 6g and 6h in good yields. The number of established intermolecular hydrogen bonds, binding energies of stable ligand-α-glucosidase complexes, and number of closest amino acid residues were determined. All the synthesized derivatives formed a complex with the target enzyme. The binding energy of docked 6h was found to be the lowest (-10.56 kcal/mol) among the energies of the docked derivatives. The inhibition activity of acarbose correlates with the number of hydroxyl groups and the number of established hydrogen bonds. Three residues appear to interact with compound 6h, Ala234, Arg552 and Asp469, to which 6h can establish hydrogen bonds.
